```{r}
#Uploading data
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")

#Exploring Variables
head(penguins)
colnames(penguins)
```

This dataset includes data about penguins, including species, island, sex, year, bill length, bill depth, flipper length, and body mass.

```{r}
#Size of dataset
nrow(penguins)
ncol(penguins)
```

This dataset contains `r nrow(penguins)` observations and `r ncol(penguins)` variables.

```{r}
#Mean flipper length
mean_flipper_length <- mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm=TRUE)
```

The mean flipper length is `r round(mean_flipper_length, 1)` mm.

```{r}
# JAS note: let's talk about spacing from the start of the line, as this can help visually to see where a specific function or command ends. 
# JAS note: We can add functions to the r inside the brackets to clean up your output, such as warning = FALSE. 

#Plot of flipper length vs. bill length, colored by species
library(ggplot2)
penguin_scatterplot <- 
ggplot(penguins, aes(x=bill_length_mm, y=flipper_length_mm, 
color= species)) + 
geom_point() +
labs(title="Penguin Flipper Length vs. Bill Length by Species",
    x = "Bill Length (mm)",
    y = "Flipper Length (mm)",
    color = "Species") +
    theme_minimal()

#Saving Plot
ggsave(
  filename = "penguin_scatterplot.png",
  plot = penguin_scatterplot,
  width = 6,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)

# JAS note: in terms of organization, this would be good to move to it's own section or R chunk, becuase it is now a separate task. 
# JAS note: for the logical vector, try: is_positive = ifelse(normal_sample > 0, TRUE, FALSE)
# JAS note: your factor doesn't always have three levels, because you've used sample, so sometimes it only has two. Could have hard coded it with different levels. 
# JAS note: these variables names are not very meaningful - e.g., fruit would be a better name for your character vector, or fruit_char

#Create dataframe
hw1_df <- data.frame(normal_sample = rnorm(10, mean = 0, sd = 1),
is_positive = logical(10),
character_vector = c("Apple", "Banana", "Cherry", "Raspberry", "Elderberry", 
                     "Fig", "Lime", "Honeydew", "Kiwi", "Lemon"),
factor_vector=factor(sample(c("Low", "Medium", "High"), 10, replace = TRUE))
)

hw1_df$is_positive <- hw1_df$normal_sample > 0

print(hw1_df)

#Calculating means
mean(hw1_df$normal_sample)
mean(hw1_df$is_positive)
mean(hw1_df$character_vector)
mean(hw1_df$factor_vector)

# JAS note: missing last part of question 2: In some cases, you can explicitly convert variables from one type to another. Write a code chunk that applies the as.numeric function to the logical, character, and factor variables (please show this chunk but not the output). What happens, and why? Does this help explain what happens when you try to take the mean?


```

The mean of the random sample from a normal distribution is `r mean(hw1_df$normal_sample)` and the mean of the logical vector indicating whether values are greater than zero is `r mean(hw1_df$is_positive)`. 
The other two means yielded a results of NA because they are not numerical variables. The logical variable mean reflects the proportion of TRUE outcomes in the dataset.
